title: Gyeongju vs Andong: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Gyeongju for first-timers and history depth. Andong for authentic Korean culture, Hahoe Folk Village, and the road less traveled. Both together make the ultimate Korean heritage route.

categories.name: Historical Sites
categories.summary: Gyeongju has more to see — Bulguksa, Seokguram, Tumuli Park, and a whole city of royal ruins.

categories.name: Authenticity
categories.summary: Andong's Hahoe Folk Village is a living UNESCO heritage site — people still reside there.

categories.name: Ease of Access
categories.summary: Gyeongju is on the KTX line near Busan; Andong requires extra transit planning.

categories.name: Budget
categories.summary: Both are affordable; Andong is slightly cheaper with fewer tourist-priced venues.

categories.name: Food Scene
categories.summary: Andong is famous for jjimdak, heotjesabap, and traditional soju — genuinely unique regional dishes.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Gyeongju is great for cycling; Andong requires buses to reach Hahoe Village (40-45 min each way).

categories.name: Crowd Level
categories.summary: Andong draws fewer tourists than Gyeongju, especially outside festival season.

categories.name: Time Required
categories.summary: Gyeongju needs 2-3 days; Andong can be done well in 1-2 days.

faq.question: Is Gyeongju or Andong better for first-time visitors to Korea?
faq.answer: Gyeongju — far more to see, easier to reach from Busan and Seoul, and the history density is unmatched in Korea.

faq.question: Can I visit both Gyeongju and Andong on the same trip?
faq.answer: Yes — they're 1.5-2 hours apart by bus and complement each other perfectly as a Korean heritage route.

faq.question: What is Andong most famous for?
faq.answer: Hahoe Folk Village (UNESCO), the Andong Mask Dance Festival, traditional Korean soju, and jjimdak (braised chicken).
